'''Anil Agarwal''' (born 1954<ref>{{Cite web |last=Crabtree |first=James |date=15 June 2013 |title=Anil Agarwal: Vedanta's bluff billionaire |url=https://www.ft.com/content/b4f90c32-f178-11e3-a2da-00144feabdc0 |work=Financial Times}}</ref>), is an Indian billionaire businessman who is the founder and chairman of [[Vedanta Resources|Vedanta Resources Limited]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.vedantaresources.com/about-us/leadership.aspx |title=Leadership |publisher=Vedanta |access-date=28 January 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150206055847/http://www.vedantaresources.com/about-us/leadership.aspx |archive-date=6 February 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://mybtechlife.com/the-list-of-great-entrepreneurs-in-india-2015/ |title=The List of Great Entrepreneurs of India in 2015 |publisher=MyBTechLife |author=Srikar Muthyala |date=29 September 2015 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160114000446/http://mybtechlife.com/the-list-of-great-entrepreneurs-in-india-2015/ |archivedate=14 January 2016 }}</ref> He controls Vedanta Resources through Volcan Investments, a holding vehicle with a 100% stake in the business.<ref name="theguardian.com">{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2010/sep/06/vedanta-human-rights-issues-india|title=Vedanta investors look into human rights issues in India|last=Moya|first=Elena|date=6 September 2010|website=the Guardian|access-date=18 January 2018|archive-date=19 January 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180119060628/https://www.theguardian.com/business/2010/sep/06/vedanta-human-rights-issues-india|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=International |first=Survival |title=Anil Agarwal - Chairman of Vedanta Resources - Survival International |url=https://www.survivalinternational.org/about/anil-agarwal |access-date=2023-05-24 |website=www.survivalinternational.org |language=en |archive-date=28 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231128170356/https://www.survivalinternational.org/about/anil-agarwal |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Early life==
Anil Agarwal was born and brought up in a [[Marwari people|Marwadi]] family in [[Patna]], [[Bihar]], [[India]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anil Agarwal: Vedanta Founder Story |url=https://startupfox.in/article/anil-agarwal-vedanta-founder-story |website=StartupFox |access-date=2026-04-03}}</ref> His father, Dwarka Prasad Agarwal, had a small aluminum conductor business.<ref name="indianexpress.2010-08-24">{{Cite news |url=http://archive.indianexpress.com/news/the-mine-millionaire/664001/|title=The mine millionaire |date=24 August 2010 |newspaper=[[The Indian Express]] |language=en-gb|access-date=10 July 2018|archive-date=8 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180708191508/http://archive.indianexpress.com/news/the-mine-millionaire/664001|url-status=dead |quote=It's a long journey for the 56-year-old [...]}}</ref><ref name="bs">{{cite web|url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/anil-agarwal-pledges-75-of-his-wealth-to-charity-114092600997_1.html|title=Anil Agarwal pledges 75% of his wealth to charity|work=Business Standard|date=27 September 2014|access-date=28 January 2015|archive-date=4 January 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150104014610/http://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/anil-agarwal-pledges-75-of-his-wealth-to-charity-114092600997_1.html|url-status=live}}</ref> He studied at Miller High School, Patna.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/opinion/lunch-with-bs-anil-agarwal-chairman-vedanta-group-113122701096_1.html |title=Lunch with BS - Anil Agarwal |work=Business Standard |date=27 December 2013 |access-date=15 February 2024 |archive-date=15 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230415020952/https://www.business-standard.com/article/opinion/lunch-with-bs-anil-agarwal-chairman-vedanta-group-113122701096_1.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.deccanherald.com/content/90635/vedanta-founder-daring-dreamer.html|title=Vedanta founder is a daring|work=Deccan Herald|date=22 August 2010|access-date=28 January 2015|archive-date=24 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924093753/http://www.deccanherald.com/content/90635/vedanta-founder-daring-dreamer.html|url-status=live}}</ref> He decided to join his father's business, making aluminium conductors instead of going to university.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2009/jul/28/anil-agarwal-profile|title=Profile - Anil Agarwal|work=The Guardian|date=28 July 2009|access-date=15 February 2024|archive-date=17 April 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230417160144/https://www.theguardian.com/business/2009/jul/28/anil-agarwal-profile|url-status=live}}</ref> At 19, Anil left Patna for [[Mumbai]] (then [[Mumbai|Bombay]]) to explore career opportunities.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rediff.com/money/2005/feb/16inter.htm |title=Don't be too smart, looking foolish is OK |publisher=Rediff Money |date=15 February 2005 |access-date=28 January 2015 |archive-date=20 September 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140920193009/http://www.rediff.com/money/2005/feb/16inter.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Career ==

In the mid-1970s, he began trading in scrap metal, collecting it from cable companies in other states and selling it in Mumbai.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bcgperspectives.com/content/videos/organization_design_human_resources_anil_agarwal_simplicity_determination_vedanta_resources/ |title=Anil Agarwal on Simplicity and Determination at Vedanta Resources |publisher=bcg.perspectives |date=11 March 2014 |access-date=28 January 2015 |archive-date=14 April 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150414151947/https://www.bcgperspectives.com/content/videos/organization_design_human_resources_anil_agarwal_simplicity_determination_vedanta_resources/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In 1976, Anil Agarwal acquired Shamsher Sterling Corporation,<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Who is Anil Agarwal |url=https://www.business-standard.com/about/who-is-anil-agarwal |access-date=15 February 2024 |archive-date=2 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240202031052/https://www.business-standard.com/about/who-is-anil-agarwal |url-status=live }}</ref> a manufacturer of enameled copper, among other products, with a [[bank loan]]. For the next 10 years, he ran both businesses. In 1986, he established a factory to manufacture jelly-filled cables, founding Sterlite Industries. He soon realised that the profitability of his business was volatile, fluctuating with the prices of his raw materials: copper and aluminium. So he decided to control his input costs by manufacturing the metals instead of buying them.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.forbes.com/2009/08/18/vedanta-resources-commodities-india-forbes-india-anil-agarwal.html/ |title=Anil Agarwal's Big Bang Theory |work=Forbes |date=18 August 2009 |access-date=15 February 2024 |archive-date=16 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230416144225/https://www.forbes.com/2009/08/18/vedanta-resources-commodities-india-forbes-india-anil-agarwal.html |url-status=live }}</ref>
 
In 1993, Sterlite Industries became the first private sector company in India to set up a copper smelter and refinery.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/magazine/cover-story/story/20100920-bold-baron-744045-2010-09-09 |title=Bold Baron |publisher=India Today |date=10 September 2010 |access-date=28 January 2015 |archive-date=4 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304072703/http://indiatoday.intoday.in/story/bold-baron/2/112119.html |url-status=live }}</ref> In 1995, Sterlite Industries acquired Madras Aluminium, a 'sick' company that had been shut down for 4 years and held by the [[Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction]] (BIFR).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.myiris.co.in/shares/company/snapShotShow.php?icode=MADALUCO |title=Madras Aluminium Company Limited |publisher=my iris |access-date=28 January 2015 |archive-date=15 August 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140815025134/http://myiris.co.in/shares/company/snapShotShow.php?icode=MADALUCO |url-status=live }}</ref> 

His first opportunity came when the government announced a [[disinvestment]] program.  In 2001, he acquired 51 percent in [[Bharat Aluminium Company]] (BALCO) for an amount of INR 551.50 crore,<ref>{{Cite news |last=Trust India |first=Press |date=March 2016 |title=Stake in HZL, Balco |work=Economic Times |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/economy/finance/government-can-get-3-7-billion-for-its-stake-in-hzl-balco-anil-agarwal/articleshow/51240709.cms |access-date=15 February 2024 |archive-date=5 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221005205710/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/economy/finance/government-can-get-3-7-billion-for-its-stake-in-hzl-balco-anil-agarwal/articleshow/51240709.cms |url-status=live }}</ref> a public sector undertaking; in the very next year, he acquired a majority stake (nearly 65 per cent) in state-run HZL(Hindustan Zinc Limited). Both companies were considered sleepy and inefficient mining firms.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2012-08-22/news/33322371_1_balco-stake-vedanta-group-hzl |title=Vedanta may offer 25% higher price for HZL, Balco stake |work=Economic Times |date=22 August 2012 |access-date=28 January 2015 |archive-date=5 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305035933/http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2012-08-22/news/33322371_1_balco-stake-vedanta-group-hzl |url-status=dead }}</ref>

To access international capital markets, Anil Agarwal and his team incorporated Vedanta Resources Plc in 2003 in London. At the time of its listing, Vedanta Resources Plc, was the first Indian firm to be listed on [[London Stock Exchange]], on 10 December 2003,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rediff.com/money/2003/dec/10vedanta.htm |title=Vedanta Resources formally lists on LSE |publisher=Rediff |date=10 December 2003 |access-date=28 January 2015 |archive-date=4 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304031118/http://www.rediff.com/money/2003/dec/10vedanta.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Vedanta Resources became the parent company of the group through a process of internal restructuring of group companies and their shareholding.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ghosh |first=Saptaparno |date=2025-07-12 |title=Explained {{!}} What was the premise of Viceroy Research’s short of Vedanta? |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/Industry/explained-what-was-the-premise-of-viceroy-researchs-short-of-vedanta/article69799840.ece |access-date=2025-09-13 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref>

Vedanta Resources, headquartered in London, is a globally diversified natural resources conglomerate, with interests in zinc, lead, silver, copper, iron ore, aluminium, power generation, and oil and gas.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.forbes.com/companies/vedanta-resources/ |title=Vedanta Resources |work=Forbes |date=May 2014 |access-date=15 February 2024 |archive-date=11 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611132801/https://www.forbes.com/companies/vedanta-resources/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The greatest share of its assets, however, is in India; Agarwal lives in London.

In October 2017, it was announced that Agrawal's Volcan Holdings Plc had taken a 19% stake in mining company [[Anglo American plc|Anglo American]], making him the biggest shareholder of the company.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.moneyweb.co.za/news-fast-news/billionaire-agarwal-increases-stake-in-anglo-american-to-19/ |title=Billionaire Agarwal increases stake in Anglo American to 19% |publisher=Bloomberg |date=October 2017 |access-date=15 February 2024 |archive-date=15 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230415015441/https://www.moneyweb.co.za/news-fast-news/billionaire-agarwal-increases-stake-in-anglo-american-to-19/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Investments in India ==
Anil Agarwal through his [[Vedanta Limited|Vedanta]] group has made several investments in various [[States and union territories of India|Indian states]].<ref name="v019">{{cite web | last=Vaitheesvaran | first=Bharani | title=Vedanta scouting across five states as semiconductor plan picks pace | website=The Economic Times | date=2022-03-22 | url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/technology/vedanta-scouting-across-five-states-as-semiconductor-plan-picks-pace/articleshow/90361572.cms | access-date=2024-11-14}}</ref>

* He had invested ₹80000 crore earlier in [[Odisha]], with an additional investment of more than ₹25000 crore for expansion of its Aluminium, Ferrochrome, and mining business in the state. Vedanta has invested nearly 4% of Odisha's GDP in 2022.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Pandey |first=Nishtha |date=Sep 15, 2022 |title=Vedanta's Anil Agarwal pumps in Rs 25,000 crore |work=CNBC TV18 |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/business/business-cartoons/vedanta-rallies-after-anil-agarwal-pumps-in-rs-25000-crore-more-in-odisha-14730811.htm |access-date=15 February 2024 |archive-date=20 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230320020631/https://www.cnbctv18.com/business/business-cartoons/vedanta-rallies-after-anil-agarwal-pumps-in-rs-25000-crore-more-in-odisha-14730811.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>
* Vedanta invested ₹1.54 lakh crore in [[Gujarat]] in association with [[Foxconn]] (2022), for their new semiconductor plant.<ref name=":0" />

== Controversy and criticism ==

In 2004, a committee of the [[Indian Supreme Court]] charged that Vedanta had dumped thousands of tons of arsenic-bearing slag near its factory in the Indian state of [[Tamil Nadu]], resulting in major poisoning of the environment and neighbouring population. In 2005, another committee of the Indian Supreme Court charged that Vedanta had forced over one hundred indigenous families from their homes in the Indian state of [[Odisha]], where it sought to mine bauxite. According to the committee's report, "An atmosphere of fear was created through the hired goons", and residents were "beaten up by the employees of M/s Vedanta". Vedanta's actions in Odisha were rebuked by the British commerce agency, and the Church of England investment funds sold their shares in the company in protest. In [[Zambia]], Vedanta dumped hazardous waste into the [[Kafue River]] from its copper mine there, according to a lawsuit filed by 2,000 residents, resulting in widespread human illness and the death of fish. A local judge stated: "This was lack of corporate responsibility and criminal, and a tipping point for corporate recklessness". In 2014, an audit was begun by Zambian officials due to suspicions that Vedanta had not been paying its proper fees to the government. In addition, "hundreds of former mine workers are fighting Vedanta for severance or disability pay."

=== Thoothukudi massacre ===
{{main article|Thoothukudi violence}}
In March and April 2018, there were renewed mass protests against the company's plans to set up a second smelting complex and to demand a shutdown of its [[Thoothukudi]] (Tuticorin) smelting plants, on grounds of violating environmental regulations. On 22 May 2018, the protests took a deadlier turn as 13 people were shot died and several others injured,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://scroll.in/article/880193/two-days-after-police-kill-13-anti-sterlite-protestors-in-thoothukudi-sorrow-and-anger-fill-the-air |title=Two days after police kill 13 anti-Sterlite protestors in Thoothukudi, sorrow and anger fill the air |publisher=scroll.in |date=28 May 2018 |access-date=15 February 2024 |archive-date=11 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230411071445/https://scroll.in/article/880193/two-days-after-police-kill-13-anti-sterlite-protestors-in-thoothukudi-sorrow-and-anger-fill-the-air |url-status=live }}</ref> following a police shooting. Section 144 was imposed to control the situation.<ref name="theguardian.com" /><ref name="nytimes.com">{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/02/08/nyregion/stream-of-foreign-wealth-flows-to-time-warner-condos.html|title=Stream of Foreign Wealth Flows to Elite New York Real Estate|last1=Story|first1=Louise|date=7 February 2015|work=The New York Times|access-date=18 January 2018|last2=Saul|first2=Stephanie|language=en-US|issn=0362-4331|archive-date=4 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210904041734/https://www.nytimes.com/2015/02/08/nyregion/stream-of-foreign-wealth-flows-to-time-warner-condos.html|url-status=live}}</ref> The Justice Aruna Jagadeesan Commission has not found any “specific evidence” that points to the involvement of either Sterlite Industries, as claimed by a few activist groups, or any outfit, as alleged by the then government and a few individuals such as actor Rajinikanth, in the violence of 22 May 2018.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://frontline.thehindu.com/news/inquiry-commission-report-on-thoothukudi-firing-names-top-police-officials-for-serious-offences-against-unarmed-civilians/article65782715.ece | title=Thoothukudi firing: Inquiry Commission report names top police officials for violations | date=18 August 2022 }}</ref>

== Philanthropy ==

In 1992, Anil Agarwal created the Vedanta Foundation as the vehicle through which the group companies would carry out their philanthropic programs and activities.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mining baron Anil Agarwal's father dies at 87; associated with Vedanta Foundation for last three decades|url=https://www.firstpost.com/business/mining-baron-anil-agarwals-father-dies-at-87-associated-with-vedanta-foundation-for-last-three-decades-7852981.html|website=Firstpost|date=2 January 2020|access-date=2020-05-13|archive-date=16 April 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230416104417/https://www.firstpost.com/business/mining-baron-anil-agarwals-father-dies-at-87-associated-with-vedanta-foundation-for-last-three-decades-7852981.html|url-status=live}}</ref> In the financial year 2013–14, the Vedanta group companies and the Vedanta foundation invested US$49.0 million in building [[hospitals]], schools and infrastructure, conserving the environment and funding community programs that improve health, education and livelihood of over 4.1 million people.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.navhindtimes.in/economic-scan-17/ |title=Sesa Sterlite wins Asian CSR Leadership Award |work=[[The Navhind Times]] |date=15 October 2014 |access-date=28 January 2015 |archive-date=17 October 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141017053154/http://www.navhindtimes.in/economic-scan-17/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The initiatives were undertaken in partnership with the government and [[non-governmental organizations]] (NGOs). Among his inspirations, Agarwal counts [[Andrew Carnegie]] and [[David Rockefeller]] who built public works with their fortunes, and [[Bill Gates]].<ref>{{Cite news|last=Satapathy|first=Bhupesh Bhandari Dillip|date=2014-12-06|title=Anil Agarwal: Charity on his mind|work=Business Standard India|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/anil-agarwal-charity-on-his-mind-114120501329_1.html|access-date=2020-05-13|archive-date=16 April 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230416174058/https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/anil-agarwal-charity-on-his-mind-114120501329_1.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=How Andrew Carnegie set the stage for Bill Gates to give away his fortune, altering philanthropy forever|url=https://www.geekwire.com/2018/andrew-carnegie-set-stage-bill-gates-give-away-fortune-changed-philanthropy-forever/|date=2018-02-08|website=GeekWire|language=en-US|access-date=2020-05-13|archive-date=16 April 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230416170433/https://www.geekwire.com/2018/andrew-carnegie-set-stage-bill-gates-give-away-fortune-changed-philanthropy-forever/|url-status=live}}</ref> The activities funded by his philanthropy are focused on child welfare, women empowerment and education.

Anil Agarwal was ranked second in the Hurun India Philanthropy List 2014 for his personal donation of Rs. 1,796 crore (about $360 million). He was ranked 25th in the Hurun India Rich List with a personal fortune of 12,316cr.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hurun.net/EN/ArticleShow.aspx?nid=213 |title=Hurun India Philanthropy List 2013 |publisher=Hurun |date=13 November 2013 |access-date=28 January 2015 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20150128055536/http://www.hurun.net/EN/ArticleShow.aspx?nid=213 |archive-date=28 January 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thetimes.com/travel/destinations/asia-travel/india/vedanta-mining-tycoon-anil-agarwal-vows-to-give-away-fortune-xmj0d6jhkvc |title=Vedanta mining tycoon Anil Agarwal vows to give away fortune |work=[[The Times]] |date=26 September 2014 |access-date=28 January 2015 |archive-date=1 December 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141201040741/http://www.thetimes.co.uk/tto/business/industries/naturalresources/article4218277.ece |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2015, the Vedanta group, in partnership with the Ministry for Women and Child development, inaugurated the first "Nand Ghar" or modern anganwadi, of the 4,000 planned to set up.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/news-ians/nand-ghar-project-launched-by-vedanta-women-and-child-ministry-115062501062_1.html|title=Nand Ghar project launched by Vedanta, women and child ministry|last=IANS|date=25 June 2015|work=Business Standard India|access-date=30 May 2018|archive-date=13 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180513084635/http://www.business-standard.com/article/news-ians/nand-ghar-project-launched-by-vedanta-women-and-child-ministry-115062501062_1.html|url-status=live}}</ref> As of 2022, a total of 3,700 "Nand Ghars" have been established across 13 states in India.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Journal |first=The CSR |date=2022-11-14 |title=CSR: Vedanta Kicks Off Feeding Drive of 2 Million Meals |url=https://thecsrjournal.in/csr-vedanta-kicks-off-feeding-drive-of-2-million-meals/ |access-date=2023-09-25 |website=The CSR Journal |language=en-GB |archive-date=29 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231129021943/https://thecsrjournal.in/csr-vedanta-kicks-off-feeding-drive-of-2-million-meals/ |url-status=live }}</ref> 

Agarwal has pledged to donate 75% of his family's wealth to charity, stating that he was inspired by [[Gates Foundation|Bill Gates]].<ref name="bs" />
‌In 2021, the  Anil Agarwal Foundation pledged to spend Rs 5000 crore on social impact programmes focused on nutrition, women & child development, healthcare, animal welfare, and grassroots-level sports over the course of 5 years.<ref>{{cite news |title=Vedanta pledges to spend Rs 5000 crore towards society in next 5 years: Anil Agarwal. |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/vedanta-pledges-to-spend-rs-5000-crore-towards-society-in-next-5-years-anil-agarwal/articleshow/84039460.cms |website=The Times of India |date=July 2021 |access-date=January 5, 2023 |archive-date=5 January 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230105180742/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/vedanta-pledges-to-spend-rs-5000-crore-towards-society-in-next-5-years-anil-agarwal/articleshow/84039460.cms |url-status=live }}</ref> In the same year, along with his daughter, Priya Agarwal, he joined the Giving Pledge.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anil Agarwal |url=https://givingpledge.org/pledger?pledgerId=422 |access-date=September 25, 2023 |website=givingpledge.org | date=14 December 2021 |archive-date=25 September 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230925171247/https://givingpledge.org/pledger?pledgerId=422 |url-status=live }}</ref> He repeated the pledge on the sudden death of his son Agnivesh in January 2026.<ref>[https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/darkest-day-of-my-life-vedanta-chairman-anil-aggarwal-after-son-passes-away-101767805415420.html 'Darkest day of my life': Vedanta chairman Anil Agarwal after son dies in skiing accident, Hindustan Times, Jan 08, 2026]</ref>

==Personal life==
Anil Agarwal married Kiran Agarwal in 1975. The couple has two children, Agnivesh Agarwal and Priya Agarwal.<ref>{{cite web |title=‘Kiran, tumhare bina…’ – Vedanta’s Anil Agarwal heartfelt wedding anniversary post for wife |url=https://www.etnownews.com/companies/kiran-tumhare-bina-vedantas-anil-agarwal-heartfelt-wedding-anniversary-post-for-wife-article-151545098 |website=Economic Times}}</ref> Their elder son, Agnivesh Agarwal, died in January 2026 at the age of 49.<ref>{{cite web |title=Agnivesh Agarwal Dies at 49, Anil Agarwal Shares Emotional Post |url=https://www.brutimes.com/news/business/agnivesh-agarwal-death |website=Bru Times News |language=en}}</ref>
